Lessons.Title: Problems with Missing Information
ExplanationParagraphs: Original 2021 Grade3 Unit6 Lesson13 addresses CCSS 3.MD.A.2 with measurement INFORMATION-GAP problems. Owner-device source lesson.html SHA256 e1ec4b423deee987687311e9dbcd56132c7fab530e3144000a972355ad006275 and preparation.html SHA256 df511ab4a66a7169822610d1008a290e56390d6d953dce92437cfa4a137759f5 were inspected alongside all THREE original student-facing sections. Publisher standalone student PDF, problem/data card blackline files and embedded illustrated card pixels have not been read as accessible local files, so no individual hidden-card numeric solutions are claimed.

Warm-up Estimation Exploration Giant Cantaloupe (10min) shows a regular cantaloupe stated to weigh BETWEEN 1 and5 kilograms, and a pictured giant prizewinning cantaloupe from 2010 Alaska State Fair. Students offer THREE estimates TOO LOW, ABOUT RIGHT and TOO HIGH for the giant fruit and explain their sizes. The source teacher suggests exploring guesses below100kg or above500kg, then MAY REVEAL the source actual winner weight 344 KILOGRAMS. The source fact344kg may be taught at synthesis but is not automatically the exact answer demanded from pupils before estimation.

Activity1 Info Gap Pumpkin Weigh-Off (20min) is a pair-based MLR4 INFORMATION GAP with MULTIPLICATION and DIVISION measurement stories. For each PAIR, the teacher prepares TWO original matched sets numbered 1 and2 from publisher blackline card master. One pupil receives Problem Card, other the corresponding Data Card. They do NOT show or read their private card to one another. Problem holder asks for only needed data; partner responds 'Why do you need to know?' and releases needed factual information after reasoned explanation. Each independently solves once enough information is acquired, and then compares when cards are shared. TEACHER REVIEWS after first set; pupils SWITCH ROLES for second set. The actual quantities printed on two publisher pumpkin problem/data cards were not available in local text; don't invent them.

Activity2 Info Gap Pig Weigh-Off (20min) repeats the SAME original partner routine with TWO NEW publisher card sets about pigs. Its mathematical contexts require ADDITION and SUBTRACTION of weights; again first pair solves its set, PAUSES for teacher review, then SWAPS roles for second set. The published card-specific original weights are not present in locally reviewed teacher HTML as text. The companion MUST preserve four source set instances in all (two pumpkin sets and two pig sets) with teacher handout/source-check state, not substitute invented cards and pretend 100% source equality.

The SOURCE STUDENT-FACING instructions contain ordered problem-holder/data-holder language including: ask 'Can you tell me ...?', data pupil asks 'Why do you need to know ...?', problem pupil responds 'I need to know ... because ...', repeat until they say 'I have enough information to solve this problem'; pupils solve independently, compare and repeat after trading roles. This information-access constraint is fundamental; displaying both teacher card texts together prematurely would defeat original task. First-party materials provide procedure and independent mathematics examples, explicitly NOT source card contents.

Original lesson synthesis asks children how to read weight story, what information is missing, choose operation and representation (tape diagram, equation, number line or base-ten), and explain choice. The original student PDF, photos/card pixel artwork, original blackline master and teacher-only Cool-down Winner, Winner are not inspected or copied. Authored tests and Stage D have NOT run, academic approval and deployment not claimed.

KeyConcepts.Title: Information gap
KeyConcepts.Definition: Two learners hold different parts of the story and must request needed quantities without exposing their own cards directly.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Ask what information is needed, explain why, share selectively, solve independently, compare.
KeyConcepts.Example: Pumpkin weigh-off: multiplication/division story details supplied only by teacher source cards.

KeyConcepts.Title: Use units and operations
KeyConcepts.Definition: Weight stories can ask total, difference, number of equal items or per-item unit mass.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Choose +,−,×,÷ only after identifying knowns and unknown.
KeyConcepts.Example: Pig original set focuses add/subtract; pumpkin original set focuses multiply/divide.

KeyConcepts.Title: Actual vs estimated weight
KeyConcepts.Definition: An initial reasonable guess may differ from teacher-revealed weight.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Give ordered estimates, then update after source reveals actual value.
KeyConcepts.Example: Teacher source may reveal giant cantaloupe344 kg.

WorkedExamples.Title: Giant cantaloupe warm-up
WorkedExamples.Question: A regular cantaloupe is1–5kg; suggest a reasonable range for prizewinning giant fruit.
Steps: Discuss relative size of original source photo.
Record three ordered guesses and reasoning.
Only after estimation teacher may reveal original344kg.
WorkedExamples.Check: Do not force 344kg as earlier estimate.

WorkedExamples.Title: Pumpkin info gap role protocol
WorkedExamples.Question: How to solve original pumpkin set without seeing partner card?
WorkedExamples.Method: Ask for a required data value and justify.
Steps: Request needed data and explain the operation.
Data card holder gives requested information; solve independently; swap next set.
WorkedExamples.Check: Blackline numeric data unverified; don't invent.

WorkedExamples.Title: Pig info gap role protocol
WorkedExamples.Question: What is different about original pig measurement story?
Steps: Ask for missing weight values and justify why.
Add/subtract as appropriate, compare with partner after card exchange.
WorkedExamples.Answer: Teacher evaluates source-specific pig card data
WorkedExamples.Check: Actual original card quantities not available in source text.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Treat the teacher's344kg revealed giant melon as a mandatory preimage estimate.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: The source is an estimation exploration open to several valid bounds.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Assess ordered guesses and explanation before revealing 344kg.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Invent four pumpkin/pig info gap card numerical tasks.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: The original blackline master is not locally inspected.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Require teacher-supplied original card data and fail closed on exact numeric parity.

CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: That removes the original information-gap reasoning objective.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Keep cards hidden until information requests and independent solutions complete.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Never trade roles after first card set.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Each source activity has two sets with explicit switch role requirement.

SummaryPoints: Warm-up: regular melon1–5kg; winner giant cantaloupe source teacher actual344kg revealed optionally AFTER open estimates.
Original Pumpkin Weigh-Off multiplication/division: two teacher-only card sets and partner role exchange.
Original Pig Weigh-Off addition/subtraction: two new card sets and role exchange.
Information gap inquiry must keep problem/data cards private before justified requests.
Source publisher cards, standalone PDF and photos not inspected; tests not run and Stage D deferred.
